supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller recorded creation of guest.rwong by tess.hart at 13:44 UTC, consistent with the alert and the help desk's authorized role creating temporary accounts.
The recorded group addition for guest.rwong was to Volunteers, matching the stated temporary-account practice; this event does not show an administrator-group addition.
The target name guest.rwong and the recorded Volunteers membership align with the organization's documented help-desk account-creation process, supporting a benign disposition.

A few minutes later, tess.hart launched dsa.msc at high integrity, and the workstation made LDAP and endpoint-mapper connections to the domain controller. This is relevant nearby activity, but these records do not show that the new account was given additional privileges or that this activity was malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The provided records show the account creation and one group-addition event, but do not establish that all account or group changes during the period are represented.
The process and network records do not show what actions were taken inside dsa.msc or whether the elevated process changed the alerted account.
claims_not_established: Whether rwong requested or received the temporary account.
Whether guest.rwong had other group memberships or account changes not represented in the provided records.
Why dsa.msc was launched at high integrity or whether any actions were taken in it.
unrelated_findings: Cisco AnyConnect's UI was launched on WS-THART-01, although the inventory says there is no VPN and remote administration is only from WS-SBYRNE-01. The records show the UI launch, not a VPN connection; review separately. (T278-00036, T278-00037, T278-00038)
